qns_content.text: Which process ensures that a particular organism is known by the same name throughout the world?

text_solutions: Nomenclature is the process of standardising the naming of organisms so that each organism is known by the same scientific name throughout the world.

qns_content.text: Which of the following taxonomic ranks is broader than class but narrower than kingdom?

text_solutions: In the taxonomic hierarchy, phylum is placed above class and below kingdom.

qns_content.text: Which of the following processes are basic to taxonomy?

text_solutions: Characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature are the basic processes involved in taxonomy.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic category comprises a group of related species having more characters in common than species belonging to other such groups?

text_solutions: A genus is an aggregate of closely related species that share more characters with one another than with species of other genera.

qns_content.text: What is the correct order of taxonomic categories from broadest to most specific?

options.text: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom

text_solutions: The hierarchy from the broadest to the most specific category is Kingdom → Phylum or Division → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes systematics from taxonomy?

options.text: Systematics also considers evolutionary relationships among organisms.
Systematics deals only with the local names of organisms.
Taxonomy considers evolutionary relationships, but systematics does not.

text_solutions: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification and also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

qns_content.text: What does the abbreviated author name written after a biological name indicate?

options.text: The country in which the organism was discovered
The scientist who first described the species
The family to which the organism belongs
The year in which the organism became extinct

text_solutions: The abbreviated author name indicates the scientist who first described the species. For example, “Linn.” in Mangifera indica Linn. indicates Linnaeus.

qns_content.text: Which of the following taxonomic categories includes organisms with the greatest number of common characteristics?

text_solutions: Species is the lowest taxonomic category. Members of a lower taxon share more characteristics than members of a higher taxon.

qns_content.text: Which category is used in plant classification in place of phylum?

text_solutions: In plants, classes with a few similar characters are assigned to the higher category called division, whereas the corresponding category in animals is phylum.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the taxonomic category “order”?

options.text: It is an assemblage of related families sharing a few similar characters.
It is an assemblage of related species with many common characters.
It is the lowest category in the taxonomic hierarchy.

text_solutions: Order is a higher taxonomic category formed by grouping related families that share a few similar characters.

qns_content.text: What is the significance of systematics in biological classification?

options.text: It deals only with assigning names to species.
It also considers evolutionary relationships among organisms.
It classifies organisms only according to their external appearance.

text_solutions: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification, and also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly represents a binomial scientific name?

text_solutions: In a biological name, the generic name begins with a capital letter and the specific epithet begins with a small letter. When printed, both words are written in italics, as in Homo sapiens.

qns_content.text: What does the term “taxon” refer to in biological classification?

options.text: A unit of classification representing a rank or category
A rule used for writing scientific names
A method used only for identifying plants

text_solutions: A taxon is a unit of classification representing a rank or category. Species, genus, family and other categories are taxa at different hierarchical levels.

qns_content.text: Which set of processes is basic to taxonomy?

text_solutions: Characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature are the basic processes involved in taxonomy.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic category contains organisms with the greatest number of common characteristics?

text_solutions: Species is the lowest category among the given options. Members of a lower taxon share more common characteristics than members of a higher taxon.

qns_content.text: What is identification in the study of living organisms?

options.text: Assigning an organism to a kingdom without describing it
Determining the organism to which a particular name is attached
Arranging all organisms according to their uses

text_solutions: Identification involves correctly describing an organism and determining the organism to which a particular name is attached.

qns_content.text: What does “Linn.” indicate in the biological name Mangifera indica Linn.?

options.text: The species belongs to the family Linnaeaceae.
The species was first described by Linnaeus.
The plant was first found in India.
The name is written in the Linnaean language.

text_solutions: The abbreviated author name written after the specific epithet indicates the scientist who first described the species. “Linn.” indicates Linnaeus.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes a genus?

options.text: It is an assemblage of related families.
It is a group of related species having several characters in common.
It is the highest category in biological classification.

text_solutions: A genus is a group of closely related species. Species within the same genus share more characters with one another than with species of other genera.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly matches an organism with its family?

text_solutions: The housefly, Musca domestica, belongs to the family Muscidae. Mango belongs to Anacardiaceae, wheat to Poaceae and humans to Hominidae.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes classification?

options.text: It assigns only local names to organisms.
It prevents organisms from being placed in taxonomic categories.
It groups organisms into convenient categories based on observable characters.

text_solutions: Classification is the process of grouping organisms into convenient categories based on easily observable characters.

qns_content.text: Which statement about Systema Naturae is correct?

options.text: It was a publication by Charles Darwin.
It was the title used by Linnaeus for his publication.
It was the international code for naming animals.
It was the earliest system based on the uses of organisms.

text_solutions: Linnaeus used Systema Naturae as the title of his publication. The word systematics is derived from the Latin word systema, meaning the systematic arrangement of organisms.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic category is directly below kingdom in animal classification?

text_solutions: In animal classification, phylum is placed directly below kingdom. In plants, the corresponding category is called division.

qns_content.text: On what basis were the earliest classifications of organisms made?

text_solutions: The earliest classifications were based on the uses of organisms because human beings needed sources of food, clothing and shelter.

qns_content.text: Which statement about the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN) is correct?

options.text: It provides principles only for naming plants.
It assigns local names to animal species.
It provides principles for the scientific naming of animals.

text_solutions: The ICZN provides internationally accepted principles for the scientific naming of animals. These principles help ensure that each organism has a single valid scientific name.

qns_content.text: Which of the following forms the basis of modern taxonomic studies?

options.text: External and internal structure, cell structure, development and ecological information

text_solutions: Modern taxonomic studies use external and internal structure, cell structure, developmental processes and ecological information.

qns_content.text: What distinguishes systematics from a study limited to naming and classification?

options.text: Systematics also considers evolutionary relationships among organisms.

text_solutions: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification and also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

qns_content.text: What does “Linn.” indicate in Mangifera indica Linn.?

options.text: The species was first described by Linnaeus.
The plant was first identified in India.

text_solutions: The abbreviated author name placed after the specific epithet indicates the scientist who first described the species. “Linn.” indicates Linnaeus.

qns_content.text: What is the correct way to write the scientific name of mango?

text_solutions: In a printed biological name, the generic name begins with a capital letter, the specific epithet begins with a small letter, and both words are italicised: Mangifera indica.

qns_content.text: What happens to the number of common characteristics as one moves from species towards kingdom?

text_solutions: As one moves from species towards kingdom, the number of common characteristics decreases. Members of lower taxa share more characteristics than members of higher taxa.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic category includes organisms with the greatest number of common characteristics?

text_solutions: Species is the lowest taxonomic category among the given options. Members of a lower taxon share more common characteristics than members of a higher taxon.

qns_content.text: What is meant by identification in the study of living organisms?

options.text: Determining the organism to which a particular name is attached
Grouping organisms only according to their economic uses
Assigning different local names to the same organism
Placing every organism directly in a kingdom

text_solutions: Identification involves correctly describing an organism and determining the organism to which a particular name is attached.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the taxonomic category “family”?

options.text: It is an assemblage of related orders.
It is a group of related genera with fewer similarities than those found within a genus.
It is the lowest category in the taxonomic hierarchy.
It consists of all the phyla belonging to a kingdom.

text_solutions: A family consists of related genera. Members grouped at the family level share fewer similarities than members grouped within the same genus or species.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly defines classification?

options.text: It is the grouping of organisms into convenient categories based on observable characters.
It is the assignment of a scientific name without describing the organism.
It is the use of only local names for organisms.
It is the study of only evolutionary relationships among organisms.

text_solutions: Classification is the process of grouping organisms into convenient categories based on easily observable characters.

qns_content.text: Which statement about binomial nomenclature is correct?

options.text: Both words of a biological name begin with capital letters.
The first word is the specific epithet and the second is the generic name.
Printed biological names are written in ordinary upright type.
The generic name begins with a capital letter and the specific epithet with a small letter.

text_solutions: In a biological name, the generic name begins with a capital letter and the specific epithet begins with a small letter. When printed, both words are italicised.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic category comprises a group of closely related species?

text_solutions: A genus is an aggregate of closely related species. Species of the same genus share more characters with one another than with species of other genera.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about systematics is incorrect?

options.text: It takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.
Its scope includes identification, nomenclature and classification.
It is restricted only to assigning scientific names to organisms.
The word systematics is derived from the Latin word systema.

text_solutions: Systematics is not restricted to assigning scientific names. Its scope includes identification, nomenclature and classification, and it also considers evolutionary relationships among organisms.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a correct statement about taxonomy?

options.text: It involves grouping organisms into different taxa.
It includes characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature.
It deals only with assigning names to organisms.
It helps organise the study of different kinds of organisms.

text_solutions: Taxonomy is not limited to naming organisms. Characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature are its basic processes.

qns_content.text: Which international code provides principles for the scientific naming of animals?

text_solutions: The International Code of Zoological Nomenclature provides internationally accepted principles for assigning scientific names to animals.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a rule of binomial nomenclature?

options.text: A biological name has a generic name and a specific epithet.
The generic name begins with a small letter.
The specific epithet begins with a small letter.
Both words are written in italics when printed.

text_solutions: The generic name begins with a capital letter, whereas the specific epithet begins with a small letter. Both words are italicised when printed.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a family in animal classification?

text_solutions: Felidae is a family that includes the genera Panthera and Felis. Panthera is a genus, Carnivora is an order and Chordata is a phylum.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the taxonomic hierarchy is incorrect?

options.text: A genus may contain one or more related species.
Related classes are grouped into a phylum in animals.
Kingdom is the highest category described in the hierarchy.

text_solutions: Order is ranked above family. The ascending hierarchy is species, genus, family, order, class, phylum or division and kingdom.

qns_content.text: Which international code provides principles and criteria for the scientific naming of plants?

text_solutions: The International Code for Botanical Nomenclature provides agreed principles and criteria for assigning scientific names to plants.

qns_content.text: Who used Systema Naturae as the title of his publication?

text_solutions: Carolus Linnaeus used Systema Naturae as the title of his publication. The word systematics is derived from the Latin word systema, meaning the systematic arrangement of organisms.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the taxonomic hierarchy is correct?

text_solutions: Species is the lowest taxonomic category. The ascending hierarchy is species, genus, family, order, class, phylum or division, and kingdom.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic category is used for plants in place of phylum?

text_solutions: In plants, classes with a few similar characters are assigned to the higher category called division. The corresponding category in animals is phylum.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly represents a family in animal classification?

text_solutions: Felidae is a family containing genera such as Panthera and Felis. Carnivora is an order.

qns_content.text: Who introduced the system of binomial nomenclature described in the chapter?

text_solutions: Carolus Linnaeus introduced the system of binomial nomenclature, in which every biological name has a generic name and a specific epithet.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between taxonomic rank and shared characteristics?

options.text: Members of lower taxa share more characteristics.
Members of higher taxa always share more characteristics.
All taxonomic categories have the same number of shared characteristics.
Members of a species share fewer characteristics than members of a kingdom.

text_solutions: Members of lower taxa share more characteristics. As one moves from species towards kingdom, the number of common characteristics decreases.

qns_content.text: What does the abbreviated author name in Mangifera indica Linn. indicate?

options.text: The plant was first found in India.
The species was first described by Linnaeus.

text_solutions: The abbreviated author name written after the specific epithet indicates the scientist who first described the species. “Linn.” indicates Linnaeus.

qns_content.text: Which combination of features is mentioned for animals placed in phylum Chordata?

options.text: A notochord and a dorsal hollow neural system

text_solutions: Animals such as fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals are included in Chordata based on common features such as a notochord and a dorsal hollow neural system.

qns_content.text: Which branch of biology deals with the characterisation, identification, nomenclature and classification of organisms?

text_solutions: Taxonomy includes characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature of organisms.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about binomial nomenclature is correct?

options.text: Each organism is given a scientific name consisting of only one word.
The specific epithet is written before the generic name.
The generic name is written first and begins with a capital letter.
Both components of a biological name begin with capital letters.

text_solutions: In binomial nomenclature, the generic name is written first and begins with a capital letter. It is followed by the specific epithet, which begins with a small letter.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic category ranks immediately above order?

text_solutions: Class ranks immediately above order. The ascending sequence is species, genus, family, order, class, phylum or division, and kingdom.

qns_content.text: Which of the following taxonomic categories is used for plants rather than animals?

text_solutions: In plants, classes with a few similar characters are assigned to the higher category called division. In animals, the corresponding category is phylum.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic category is an assemblage of related families sharing a few similar characters?

text_solutions: Order is a higher taxonomic category formed by grouping related families that share a few similar characters. For example, Carnivora includes Felidae and Canidae.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly represents a plant family mentioned in the chapter?

text_solutions: Solanaceae is a family containing related genera such as Solanum, Petunia and Datura.

qns_content.text: What is meant by identification in the study of organisms?

options.text: Assigning several local names to an organism
Placing every organism directly in a kingdom
Determining the organism to which a particular name is attached

text_solutions: Identification involves correctly describing an organism and determining the organism to which a particular name is attached.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly defines a species?

options.text: A group of organisms occupying the same habitat
A group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities
A group containing all organisms of a kingdom

text_solutions: A species is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities. Closely related species can be distinguished from one another by distinct morphological differences.

qns_content.text: Which of the following taxonomic categories includes the greatest number of species?

text_solutions: Kingdom is the highest and broadest category among the given options. It includes organisms belonging to different phyla or divisions and therefore contains the greatest number of species.

qns_content.text: Which of the following scientific names is written correctly?

text_solutions: In a printed biological name, the generic name begins with a capital letter, the specific epithet begins with a small letter, and both words are italicised: Panthera tigris.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about binomial nomenclature is incorrect?

options.text: The specific epithet is written before the generic name.
Biological names are generally in Latin or Latinised.
The system was given by Carolus Linnaeus.

text_solutions: The generic name is written first and is followed by the specific epithet. For example, in Panthera tigris, Panthera is the generic name and tigris is the specific epithet.

qns_content.text: Why is biological classification necessary?

options.text: It groups organisms into convenient categories and facilitates their study.
It prevents the identification of new organisms.
It assigns names only to economically useful organisms.

text_solutions: Because it is nearly impossible to study all organisms individually, classification groups them into convenient categories based on observable characters and facilitates their study.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic category ranks immediately above genus?

text_solutions: Family ranks immediately above genus. A family consists of related genera that share fewer similarities than the species grouped within a genus.

qns_content.text: What does the term “taxon” represent in biological classification?

options.text: A rule used for writing biological names
A unit of classification representing a rank or category
A group based only on the economic uses of organisms

text_solutions: A taxon is a unit of classification representing a rank or category. Species, genus, family and order are examples of taxa at different hierarchical levels.

qns_content.text: Why are scientific names preferred over local names?

options.text: Scientific names are always shorter than local names.
They provide a universally accepted name for each organism.
Local names cannot be used for plants.
They indicate the complete evolutionary history of an organism.

text_solutions: Local names vary from place to place. Scientific nomenclature ensures that a particular organism is known by the same name throughout the world, avoiding confusion.

qns_content.text: Which category contains organisms with the greatest number of common characteristics?

text_solutions: Species is the lowest category among the given options. Members of lower taxa share more common characteristics than members of higher taxa.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes systematics?

options.text: It deals only with assigning scientific names.
It includes identification, nomenclature and classification and considers evolutionary relationships.
It excludes the study of relationships among organisms.

text_solutions: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification and also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly describes classification?

options.text: It groups organisms into convenient categories based on observable characters.
It has no role in the study of biological diversity.
It is based only on the economic importance of organisms.

text_solutions: Classification is the process of grouping organisms into convenient categories based on easily observable characters, making their study manageable.

qns_content.text: Which statement about the language of biological names is correct?

options.text: Biological names must be written in the local language.
Only plant names are written in Latin.
Biological names are generally in Latin or are Latinised, irrespective of their origin.
The generic name and specific epithet must come from different languages.

text_solutions: Biological names are generally in Latin or are Latinised irrespective of their origin. When printed, they are written in italics.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly represents the taxonomic hierarchy in descending order?

options.text: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Kingdom → Class → Phylum → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Species → Genus → Family → Order → Phylum → Class → Kingdom
Kingdom → Phylum → Family → Order → Class → Genus → Species

text_solutions: The descending hierarchy in animals is Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species. In plants, division is used in place of phylum.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes a species?

options.text: It is a group of related genera.
It is the highest category of classification.
It is a group of organisms occupying the same habitat.
It is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities.

text_solutions: A species is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities. One species can be distinguished from a closely related species by distinct morphological differences.

qns_content.text: Panthera and Felis are placed together in Felidae. What does this demonstrate?

options.text: A family contains related genera with some common characteristics.

text_solutions: A family is a group of related genera. Felidae includes the related genera Panthera and Felis.

qns_content.text: Who gave the system of binomial nomenclature described in the chapter?

text_solutions: Carolus Linnaeus gave the system of binomial nomenclature, in which each biological name has a generic name and a specific epithet.

qns_content.text: Felidae and Canidae are placed together in which higher taxonomic category?

text_solutions: Felidae and Canidae are related families included in the order Carnivora. An order is an assemblage of families sharing a few similar characters.

qns_content.text: What is the taxonomic status of Panthera tigris?

options.text: It is the biological name of a species.

text_solutions: Panthera tigris is the biological name of the tiger species. Panthera is the generic name, while tigris is the specific epithet.

qns_content.text: Which combination of information forms the basis of modern taxonomic studies?

options.text: Only the economic uses and local names of organisms
External and internal structure, cell structure, development and ecological information

text_solutions: Modern taxonomic studies use external and internal structure, cell structure, developmental processes and ecological information.

qns_content.text: Why is standardised scientific nomenclature necessary?

options.text: It ensures that a particular organism is known by the same name throughout the world.
It permits every region to assign a different scientific name.
It eliminates the need to identify an organism.
It restricts biological names to economically useful organisms.

text_solutions: Local names vary from place to place. Standardised nomenclature ensures that a particular organism is known by the same scientific name throughout the world.

qns_content.text: An organism is moved from its species category towards its kingdom. Which change is expected?

text_solutions: As one moves from species towards kingdom, categories become broader and the number of common characteristics shared by their members decreases.

qns_content.text: Why is classification necessary for studying living organisms?

options.text: It groups organisms into convenient categories because studying all organisms individually is nearly impossible.
It restricts biological study to familiar organisms.
It groups organisms only according to their economic uses.

text_solutions: Because it is nearly impossible to study all living organisms individually, classification groups them into convenient categories and makes their study manageable.

qns_content.text: A student identifies an organism as wheat. Which combination of taxonomic categories correctly represents wheat?

text_solutions: Wheat is Triticum aestivum. It belongs to the genus Triticum, family Poaceae and order Poales.

qns_content.text: An investigator first groups organisms into convenient categories and then assigns scientific names after identifying them. Which conclusion is correct?

text_solutions: Classification, identification and nomenclature are basic processes of taxonomy. Characterisation is also included in taxonomic studies.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about nomenclature is correct?

options.text: Each organism may have several accepted scientific names.
Scientific nomenclature ensures that an organism is known by the same name throughout the world.
Scientific names change with the local language of a region.
Nomenclature can be completed without correctly describing the organism.

text_solutions: Standardised nomenclature ensures that a particular organism is known by the same scientific name throughout the world, avoiding confusion caused by different local names.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about systematics is correct?

options.text: It includes identification, nomenclature and classification and considers evolutionary relationships.
It is restricted to the assignment of scientific names.
It does not consider relationships among organisms.

text_solutions: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification. It also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic rank is the lowest category that can include organisms belonging to different genera but sharing common characteristics?

text_solutions: A family is a group of related genera. For example, the genera Panthera and Felis are included in the family Felidae.

qns_content.text: Potato, brinjal and black nightshade have the specific epithets tuberosum, melongena and nigrum, respectively. What can be inferred from the chapter?

options.text: All three belong to the same species.
All three belong to the family Felidae.

text_solutions: Solanum includes species with specific epithets such as tuberosum, melongena and nigrum. They are different species belonging to the same genus.

qns_content.text: A human is classified under Hominidae and Mammalia. Which category lies between these two ranks?

text_solutions: Hominidae is the family, Primata is the order and Mammalia is the class of humans. Therefore, Primata lies between Hominidae and Mammalia.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the handwritten form of a biological name?

options.text: The generic name and specific epithet are underlined separately.
Both words are enclosed within quotation marks.
The two words are joined and underlined as one unit.

text_solutions: When a biological name is handwritten, the generic name and specific epithet are underlined separately. When printed, both words are written in italics.

qns_content.text: Which of the following taxonomic categories contains organisms with the fewest common characteristics?

text_solutions: Kingdom is the highest and broadest category among the given options. As one moves from species towards kingdom, the number of common characteristics decreases.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN)?

options.text: It provides principles for assigning scientific names only to plants.
It provides internationally accepted principles for the scientific naming of animals.
It permits the same scientific name to be assigned to different known animals.
It replaces the binomial system of nomenclature in animals.

text_solutions: The ICZN provides internationally accepted principles for assigning scientific names to animals. Such naming procedures help ensure that each organism has a distinct scientific name.

qns_content.text: Which taxonomic category includes the fewest organisms among the following?

text_solutions: Species is the lowest and most specific category among the given options. Lower categories include fewer organisms whose members share more characteristics.

qns_content.text: A human is placed in the family Hominidae and the class Mammalia. Which category lies between these two ranks?

text_solutions: Humans belong to the family Hominidae, order Primata and class Mammalia. Therefore, Primata lies between Hominidae and Mammalia.

qns_content.text: Panthera and Felis are grouped together in Felidae. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: Felidae is an order containing related families.
Felidae is a family containing related genera.
Felidae is a genus containing related species.
Felidae is a class containing related orders.

text_solutions: A family contains related genera. The genera Panthera and Felis are included in the family Felidae.

qns_content.text: Which combination forms the basis of modern taxonomic studies?

options.text: External and internal structure, cell structure, development and ecological information

text_solutions: Modern taxonomic studies use external and internal structure, cell structure, developmental processes and ecological information.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes systematics from a study limited to nomenclature?

options.text: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification and also considers evolutionary relationships.
Systematics is limited only to assigning scientific names.
Systematics considers only the economic uses of organisms.

text_solutions: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification. It also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

qns_content.text: Which combination of taxonomic categories correctly represents wheat?

text_solutions: Wheat is Triticum aestivum. It belongs to the genus Triticum, family Poaceae and order Poales.

qns_content.text: Which international code provides agreed principles and criteria for the scientific naming of plants?

text_solutions: The International Code for Botanical Nomenclature provides agreed principles and criteria for assigning scientific names to plants.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly explains the term “taxon”?

options.text: It refers only to the species category.
It is a rule for writing biological names.
It is a unit of classification representing a rank or category.
It refers only to groups of animals.

text_solutions: A taxon is a unit of classification representing a rank or category. Species, genus, family and class are taxa at different hierarchical levels.

qns_content.text: Which statement about species is correct?

options.text: A species is an assemblage of related genera.
A species is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities.
Every species belongs to several different genera.
Closely related species cannot be distinguished morphologically.

text_solutions: A species is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities. Closely related species can be distinguished from one another by distinct morphological differences.

qns_content.text: Felidae and Canidae share a few similar characters and are placed together in which category?

text_solutions: Felidae and Canidae are related families placed in the order Carnivora. An order is an assemblage of families sharing a few similar characters.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the scope of systematics?

options.text: It deals only with assigning names to organisms.
It includes identification, nomenclature and classification and considers evolutionary relationships.
It groups organisms only according to their economic uses.

text_solutions: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification. It also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

qns_content.text: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between phylum and class in animal classification?

options.text: Class and phylum represent the same rank.

text_solutions: Related classes are grouped into a phylum in animal classification. For example, classes containing fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals are included in Chordata.

qns_content.text: A human is classified under the genus Homo and the order Primata. Which category lies between these two ranks?

text_solutions: Humans belong to the genus Homo, family Hominidae and order Primata. Therefore, Hominidae lies between the genus and order.

qns_content.text: Solanum tuberosum, Solanum melongena and Solanum nigrum illustrate which taxonomic principle?

options.text: A specific epithet can be used without a generic name.
All organisms in a genus have the same specific epithet.
A genus may include several related species.

text_solutions: The genus Solanum includes several related species with different specific epithets, such as tuberosum, melongena and nigrum.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about classification is incorrect?

options.text: It may use easily observable characters for grouping organisms.
It makes the study of the large diversity of organisms manageable.
It is applicable only to animals and not to plants.

text_solutions: Classification applies to all organisms, including plants and animals. It groups organisms into convenient categories and makes their study manageable.

qns_content.text: Which combination of taxonomic categories correctly represents mango?

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly represents the taxonomic hierarchy from lowest to highest?

options.text: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom

Species → Family → Genus → Class → Order → Phylum → Kingdom
Order → Family → Genus → Class → Species → Phylum → Kingdom

text_solutions: The ascending hierarchy in animals is Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom. In plants, division is used in place of phylum.

qns_content.text: Felidae and Canidae share a few similar characters. In which higher category are these families placed together?

text_solutions: Felidae and Canidae are related families included in the order Carnivora. An order is an assemblage of families that share a few similar characters.

The generic name begins with a small letter.

text_solutions: The generic name begins with a capital letter, whereas the specific epithet begins with a small letter. When handwritten, the two words are underlined separately.

text_solutions: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification. It also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

qns_content.text: Which of the following taxonomic categories is the most specific?

text_solutions: Species is the lowest and most specific taxonomic category. Its members share more characteristics than members grouped at higher taxonomic levels.

qns_content.text: Which option correctly represents the taxonomic position of humans as given in the chapter?

qns_content.text: An organism is considered successively at the species, genus, family and kingdom levels. Which change is expected as one moves towards kingdom?

text_solutions: As one moves from species towards kingdom, the categories become broader and the number of common characteristics decreases. Determining relationships among taxa at higher levels also becomes more difficult.

qns_content.text: Which combination of taxonomic categories correctly represents the housefly?

A family always contains only one genus.

options.text: Categories become narrower and common characteristics increase.
Categories become narrower and relationships become easier to determine.
Common characteristics increase and fewer organisms are included.
Categories become broader and common characteristics decrease.

The tiger and lion belong to different families.

tuberosum alone is the complete scientific name of the species.
